channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-24
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 99 news received.

item.title: Jensen Huang’s return upends the rules of work
item.description: Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sends the message that some executives do not have to follow the rules.

item.title: Claude Ship automates GitHub code reviews with agents
item.description: Claude Ship automates GitHub code reviews by deploying agents. The tool is presented as a way to accelerate development.

item.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist calls for limits on the pace of AI progress
item.description: Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores for every major model since GPT-3.5 and is asking competing labs to agree on common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.

item.title: A visualization of the Riemann proof goes viral
item.description: A visualization maps the 17 million lines of the Riemann proof. Its shape is strikingly reminiscent of the human central nervous system.

item.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
item.description: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, bringing together endpoint protection, zero-trust networking, cloud security, and threat intelligence. Jay Chaudhry will remain CEO of Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.

item.title: OpenAI deploys GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT’s Chat tab
item.description: OpenAI is adding a chat-optimized version of GPT-6.2 Sol to ChatGPT’s Chat tab. Sol and Astra are also available in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API; OpenAI says Sol delivers performance close to Astra’s at about one-fifth the cost.

item.title: Shirudo, OpenAI and Cisco’s open-source tool, protects Linux servers
item.description: Shirudo is a free, open-source tool that protects a Linux server against a known exploit until the permanent patch is installed, without requiring a restart. Operators must approve each protection.

item.title: OpenAI withdrew its AI detector because of its low accuracy
item.description: OpenAI says it withdrew its AI-generated text detection tool in July 2023 because of its low accuracy.

item.title: OpenAI launches OpenWorks to help small businesses adopt AI
item.description: OpenWorks offers a monthly allocation of up to $8,000 to AI experts who help small businesses achieve their goals with the technology. The pilot program covers 20 U.S. communities and targets restaurants, retailers, and service businesses in particular.

item.title: Former OpenAI engineer allegedly recorded trade secrets
item.description: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, pleaded not guilty after allegedly spying on a conference room, possibly to intercept trade secrets. Hundreds of audio files were found on his computer, some of which appear to have been uploaded to Dropbox.

item.title: Nvidia rivals are designing chips with artificial intelligence
item.description: OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are using AI models to design chips that could replace Nvidia GPUs. This development poses a significant risk to the company’s dominance.

item.title: Saudi engineer allegedly used an OpenAI app to booby-trap his workplace
item.description: Federal authorities say a Saudi engineer used OpenAI’s programming application to booby-trap his company’s facilities more effectively.

item.title: Tesla unveils an FSD display that generates an AI video of the road
item.description: Tesla’s new FSD display generates an AI video representing the road while driving.

item.title: Virginia and Oregon sue Elon Musk’s companies
item.description: Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s companies, alleging that Grok lacked adequate safeguards against child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate images. These are allegations, not judicial findings.

item.title: AWS launches Strands Decider v2 to rank options
item.description: Strands Decider v2 is a family of open-weight models from AWS that scores a list of options. AWS says routing between two Claude models solves 94% of tasks at 44% of the cost.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra produces a mathematical proof using its own strategy
item.description: OpenAI’s model independently produced a computer-verifiable proof of the Smoktunowicz gap theorem. It had to invent a proof strategy because Mathlib lacked sufficient foundations and solved 49 of 56 tasks on the Autoform-Hard benchmark.

item.title: OpenAI’s AI smartphone could redefine mobile interfaces
item.description: OpenAI’s AI smartphone, reportedly to be assembled by Foxconn, would include agent-driven tasks, two NPUs, and custom hardware. Its launch is targeted for 2027-2028, raising questions about privacy, permissions, and enterprise device management.

item.title: Guide: Set up ChatGPT in five minutes
item.description: The guide explains how to enable custom instructions, provide context, and turn on memory so ChatGPT can better adapt to its user.

item.title: Create AI agents with no prior knowledge
item.description: This article explains how to build artificial intelligence agents without prior experience.

item.title: Build an AI agent in minutes with Claude
item.description: The article shows how to quickly build an artificial intelligence agent using Claude.

item.title: Create AI agents with Notion
item.description: The article explains how to create artificial intelligence agents with Notion.

item.title: Anthropic stages a record-breaking IPO
item.description: Anthropic is presented as having completed an IPO that broke all records.

item.title: A 10-minute test reveals the limits of AI detectors
item.description: A list of 50 words generated by Claude is classified as 100% AI-written, while a manually typed list is classified as human-written. The experiment shows that detectors analyze statistical patterns and habits rather than a hidden watermark.

item.title: Pangram explains how its detector distinguishes human and AI text
item.description: Pangram describes how the detector used in the test works and explains, according to its designers, how it differentiates human text from AI-generated text.

item.title: Google DeepMind demonstrates how the SynthID watermark works
item.description: Google DeepMind presents SynthID as a genuine deliberate text watermark and explains why it becomes less effective when the text is heavily rewritten.

item.title: TechCrunch catalogs clues that reveal AI-generated text
item.description: TechCrunch presents the guide created by volunteer Wikipedia editors on expressions and habits that can reveal machine-produced text.

item.title: Bowdoin advises against grading students based on a detection score
item.description: Bowdoin College explains why instructors should not evaluate a student solely on the score provided by an AI detector.

item.title: Adobe Firefly helps create campaign assets for social media
item.description: Firefly AI Assistant can turn a creative brief and reference images into assets for different channels. Users can define their styles and colors, approve a multi-step plan, and then refine the elements with Adobe’s creative tools.

item.title: LLMs can simulate consumer reactions with about 90% reliability
item.description: A Colgate-Palmolive study shows that LLMs can act as consumers to support market research. Across 9,300 human responses, the SSR method achieved about 90% reliability when the simulated individuals’ demographic characteristics were included.

item.title: A Claude prompt is presented as capable of speeding up a Wi-Fi network
item.description: A Datadog engineer claims that Claude can be asked to easily optimize a Wi-Fi network. The prompt also produces a before-and-after comparison to verify the result.

item.title: Microsoft’s massive outage exposes testing and capacity flaws
item.description: Microsoft’s final report explains that a Windows defect went unnoticed for months before overwhelming Microsoft 365 gateway servers. More than 80% of North American gateway servers stopped responding at the height of the outage.

item.title: Europe strengthens its cloud sovereignty requirements
item.description: European governments and regulated industries are incorporating more digital sovereignty requirements into cloud contracts to reduce their dependence on U.S. providers. Despite several contracts won by European or hybrid providers, migration remains slow because of incumbent providers’ entrenched position and the difficulties of transitioning.

item.title: AI is changing the build-versus-buy trade-off for software
item.description: AI-assisted development tools and vibe coding reduce creation costs without eliminating security, maintenance, and integration expenses. CIOs should selectively reassess developing specialized, non-critical SaaS applications rather than replacing core platforms.

item.title: Should Apple really speed up at the risk of compromising reliability?
item.description: As Apple faces pressure to accelerate its AI development, its cautious engineering culture could be an advantage. Unreliable AI features integrated into the operating system would have greater consequences than chatbot errors, reinforcing the importance of reliability, privacy, and customer trust.

item.title: AI influenced the release of PostgreSQL 19
item.description: AI-assisted testing uncovered numerous defects during the development of PostgreSQL 19, contributing to the delay in its release. The experience shows that human validation, architectural decisions, and quality assurance remain critical bottlenecks.

item.title: AWS Systems Manager now automates tasks in Azure and Google Cloud
item.description: AWS has extended Systems Manager Automation to multicloud environments. IT teams can centralize configuration remediation, resource cleanup, agent deployment, and infrastructure changes without managing separate automation workflows.

item.title: Slack launches Slackbot, an AI powered by Claude and billed at a flat rate
item.description: Slack launched Slackbot powered by Claude, with flat per-person pricing in Enterprise+ plans to eliminate token-based usage costs. Slack says this model avoids unpredictable bills and makes daily AI use easier.

item.title: AWS launches CloudWatch Omni to monitor AI agents and infrastructure
item.description: Amazon launched CloudWatch Omni, an AI-powered observability solution based on open standards and offered outside the AWS console. It unifies monitoring of AI agents, applications, and infrastructure across mult-account environments, with IDE integration and natural-language queries.

item.title: Workday completes acquisition of C1.ai in identity governance
item.description: Workday completed its acquisition of C1.ai, formerly ConductorOne, expanding into identity governance. The combination is intended to help organizations automate provisioning, permission management, and security controls for employees and AI agents.

item.title: Security providers strengthen access controls for AI agents
item.description: Security providers are developing access control, monitoring, and testing tools to address the specific risks of autonomous AI agents in the enterprise. CrowdStrike, Okta, and Cisco are seeking in particular to prevent unauthorized actions and confused-deputy scenarios, while groups are working to coordinate standards.

item.title: Amazon acquires technology to make better use of AI accelerators
item.description: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s AI optimization technology and engineering talent to improve the utilization of Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and AWS Trainium chips. The goal is to accelerate inference, increase throughput, and reduce AI computing costs.

item.title: A new Outlook attachment problem sends users back to the old version
item.description: Microsoft recommends returning to classic Outlook or its web client after a software update caused attachment-handling problems.

item.title: A Cisco remote-code-execution flaw is being exploited
item.description: CISA added a critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability affecting clustered deployments to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

item.title: AWS CodeDeploy can now pause EC2 Auto Scaling processes
item.description: AWS is introducing controls to temporarily suspend Auto Scaling activities during application deployments. This feature prevents instances from being replaced in the middle of an update.

item.title: Tesla is betting on FSD v15 to make AI4 autonomous
item.description: FSD v15 may be Tesla’s last real chance to achieve unsupervised autonomous driving on the AI4 computer. The A15 chip will not be installed in cars, and the AI4.5 upgrade has had its memory reduced from 32 to 24 GB.

item.title: A natural DNA-repair mechanism enables gene editing
item.description: Cells have a mechanism that recognizes and replaces defective DNA before it causes lasting damage. Scientists use these natural mechanisms to insert, delete, or modify genes to study and treat diseases.

item.title: Developers share methods for dealing with AI-related overload
item.description: One participant suggests having agents test multiple options, letting them perform reversible actions, and asking for help with choices that are difficult to undo. Another has agents send a daily selection of questions to a reMarkable tablet.

item.title: Declare turns prototypes into structured, verifiable applications
item.description: Declare is an interface language designed for humans and AI agents. It allows users to describe designs directly in code and provides examples of applications created with the language.

item.title: Watching users helps improve products
item.description: Watching a real user perform tasks often reveals problems that cannot be anticipated through thought alone. Fear of feedback and difficulty recognizing flaws in one’s own product can lead to poor decisions.

item.title: The open-source Ladybird browser and web engine reaches alpha
item.description: After four years of development, Ladybird, an open-source desktop browser with its own web engine, has entered alpha. It is still barely usable and some sites may crash, but macOS and Linux versions are available.

item.title: Fictional charts illustrate the prospects for human emancipation
item.description: Humanity can follow a path toward prosperity and sovereignty, but this evolution will not happen automatically.

item.title: Modernizing legacy software with LLMs is being evaluated
item.description: The first generation of a translation of more than half a million lines of code costs about $1,100 at API rates.

item.title: Coding agents spend most of their time waiting
item.description: A developer found that his Claude Code agents were working only about 26% of the time.

item.title: The community shares the most useful system prompt rules
item.description: One rule—perform reversible actions first, then report them—reduced routine decisions. Another, which recommends revising only when there is new evidence or a new argument, limits changes in Claude’s opinion.

item.title: Morgan Stanley bets on four trades for an S&P 500 rebound
item.description: Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley’s chief investment officer, is optimistic about a major rebound in the S&P 500. The bank presents four trades it is betting on.

item.title: Figma engineer accuses HR of minimizing her harassment
item.description: A Figma software engineer alleges in a complaint that two colleagues sexually harassed her and that human resources told her to handle the problem herself. Figma calls the allegations unfounded.

item.title: Highly popular Squishies toys can cause severe burns
item.description: Squishies are among the toys most in demand among children, but some have caused severe burns. Parents are urging families to choose them carefully.

item.title: A map shows the U.S. states where housing is keeping up with population growth
item.description: The number of households is increasing in several U.S. states, driving greater demand for housing. A map shows where supply is and is not meeting projected population growth.

item.title: A Ukrainian naval drone strike targets a Russian ship in Libya
item.description: Satellite images show a Ukrainian naval drone strike on a Russian warship in Libya, more than 1,600 kilometers from the war theater.

item.title: A former dishwasher becomes the owner of a $10.5 million food-truck empire
item.description: An entrepreneur recounts his journey from washing dishes to owning a food-truck empire valued at $10.5 million.

item.title: Trump suspends project to destroy explosive materials in Iowa
item.description: The U.S. Army’s plan to detonate explosive materials in Iowa became complicated. Donald Trump intervened to suspend it.

item.title: The most extravagant national costumes of Miss Universe 2026
item.description: A selection showcases the most extravagant national costumes from the Miss Universe 2026 pageant.

item.title: Google envisions an AI-generated TV channel where you are the star
item.description: A Google patent describes “My Channel,” an endless stream of AI-generated videos tailored to the viewer’s tastes and personal information. A system could integrate ads directly into each video, but Google has not said it plans to launch the product.

item.title: Coding agents poorly reuse companies’ approved code
item.description: A DesignVerse study of 15 legacy codebases found that two coding agents used approved internal code in only 55% to 59% of tasks, compared with 92% using DesignVerse’s configuration. The results should be interpreted cautiously because the study was funded by the company and its participating organizations were not named.

item.title: Anthropic allows local storage of Mythos and Fable data
item.description: Anthropic is loosening its data-retention rules for Mythos and Fable. Business customers can now retain the required prompts and responses themselves for 30 days.

item.title: Sierra raises $1.75 billion at a $30 billion valuation
item.description: The startup Sierra raised $1.75 billion, doubling its valuation in six months to $30 billion. It says nearly half of Fortune 50 companies are customers.

item.title: OpenRouter warns of possible third-party access to MiniMax conversations
item.description: OpenRouter warned that prompts and responses sent to MiniMax models may have been accessed by a third party, according to Axios.

item.title: Embo raises $110 million to train robotic models
item.description: Embo raised $110 million in a seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company develops AI models for robots trained on videos and practice in learned world models.

item.title: Google AI Mode can now analyze your Drive and Wallet files
item.description: Google AI Mode can read Drive and Wallet files to answer requests based on user data, such as building a tax plan from spreadsheets. Access is optional, and Wallet remains read-only.

item.title: The Gemini API now charges only for pages or cells used
item.description: The Gemini API lets developers send only the necessary pages or cells instead of an entire file, with billing limited to that portion. It also directly accepts Office files.

item.title: Google tests semantic governance rules for AI agents
item.description: Google’s semantic governance policies check every action proposed by an AI agent against clear-language rules before execution. The feature is in preview.

item.title: Nothing Ear Note earbuds put a microphone in their case
item.description: Nothing Ear Note earbuds place a microphone in their charging case to record and transcribe conversations. Their launch is planned for December.

item.title: Gemini 4 agents speed up quantum algorithms by up to 290 times
item.description: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of Gemini 4 agents to optimize and prove quantum algorithms. Some routines are up to 290 times faster, with results verified in Lean 4 and released as open source.

item.title: GLM-5.4 uses a looping architecture to compete with larger models
item.description: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter model whose some layers are run twice on each pass. The company claims it reaches the level of 2,000- to 3,000-billion-parameter models, but the available benchmarks cover only a test version with 30 billion parameters.

item.title: Meta’s AI chief says superintelligence is near
item.description: Alexandr Wang says AI-assisted progress on the Riemann hypothesis shows that raw intelligence is no longer the main limiting factor. Anthropic improved a mathematical bound without solving the hypothesis, while Stanford published a human proof draft.

item.title: Nvidia aims to make a speaking brain implant portable
item.description: A Paradromics implant allows a person with motor neuron disease to communicate using more than 400 electrodes and AI. An Nvidia Jetson module is expected to reduce the electronics to a wheelchair-mounted box within a year, and potentially to a phone later.

item.title: Meta’s open models help locate epilepsy seizures
item.description: Meta is funding teams using Muse Glimmer, SAM 3, DINOv3, and Brain2Qwertyv2, among others. In France, these models help doctors locate the source of epilepsy seizures, while a U.S. project trains healthcare workers in virtual reality.

item.title: RoboTrack evaluates tracking of objects manipulated by robots
item.description: Ai2 released a benchmark containing 307 annotated real-world videos, 15 million simulated trajectories, and two models. The results show that tracking is less reliable in the real world, but training on simulated data improves performance.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 costs three times more than Opus 5.5 for a similar result
item.description: In a bug-fixing test, Fable 5.2 succeeded on 10 of 15 attempts for about $89, compared with 9 of 15 for about $29 with Opus 5.5. With a larger budget, Opus also reached 10 successes for $33.

item.title: AI could become conscious in the next few years, philosopher says
item.description: Rob Long of Eleos AI says AI systems could become conscious in the next few years. He highlights the dilemma between the moral risk of ignoring it and the risk of overprotecting a dangerous agent.

item.title: Thomas Nagel challenges Anthropic’s argument about AI consciousness
item.description: Philosopher Thomas Nagel called Anthropic’s argument concerning the possible consciousness of its models “ridiculous”; the possibility is listed among risks to investors. A poll indicates that 33% of Americans think AI will become conscious and 7% think it already is.

item.title: Developer recounts how AI assistants are transforming the profession
item.description: In a personal essay published by Wired, a former philosophy student turned developer describes his relationship with code, from Java to Haskell. He reflects on a profession transformed by AI assistants.

item.title: Carbon capture through rocks could reduce crop yields
item.description: CarbonPlan studies indicate that excessive application of crushed rock to fields would reduce agricultural yields. The capture potential would be below one billion tons of CO2 per year, compared with the expected 3 to 8 billion tons.

item.title: NariQ compresses a 27-billion-parameter model into 10 GB
item.description: Nari Labs compressed Qwen3.8-27B to three bits, producing a model of about 10 GB with no measurable quality loss in several tests. The two-bit version, however, loses significant quality and requires a modified version of llama.cpp.

item.title: Gemini can now create short animated GIFs
item.description: The Gemini app can generate short looping GIFs from a description or image using the Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash model. The feature can animate a photo or create a reaction for social media.

item.title: U.S. agencies were monitoring Alice Huang in the Nvidia case
item.description: The New York Times reports that U.S. agencies were tracking Alice Huang’s contacts with China’s Ministry of State Security. Investigators are seeking, among other things, to determine whether Southeast Asian companies helped transfer banned AI chips to China.

item.title: China’s military fears AI could threaten its nuclear missiles
item.description: According to The New York Times, Chinese military researchers estimate that AI could reduce U.S. decision-making time from 15 to 30 minutes to 90 seconds. An AI-generated false report had already nearly triggered a confrontation with a Chinese ship.

item.title: AI’s energy demand revives geothermal power
item.description: Google has committed to obtaining 50 megawatts of geothermal electricity from Quaise Energy. The company must drill nearly five kilometers beneath Oregon to reach very hot rock and produce steam for turbines.

item.title: xAI rents its servers to Anthropic and Google instead of building everything itself
item.description: Since May, SpaceXSI, xAI’s parent company, has reportedly been renting computing power to its own competitors. Meanwhile, xAI is scaling back its projects and dissolved the 60-person Grok Imagine team after going public.

item.title: AI-assisted attack takes European Commission systems offline
item.description: An AI-driven intrusion forced the European Commission to take its human-resources and reimbursement systems offline for ten days. The attack illustrates the speed enabled by public tools such as ARTEX and the importance of defenses, segmentation, and continuity plans.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon cuts the cost of AI-assisted coding
item.description: Google Gemini 4 Neon handles bugs spread across multiple files with a one-million-token context and four reasoning levels. The very high level increases costs by about 72% for minimal gains.

item.title: A GTA 6 Scam Kit Is Circulating for $200
item.description: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are linked to a $200 scam kit containing account stealers, cryptocurrency drainers, and hidden miners. The article outlines warning signs and immediate steps to protect accounts and devices.

item.title: Nvidia’s AI Computers Could Reduce Cloud Costs
item.description: Nvidia’s RTX Spark desktop computers come with up to 128 GB of memory to run models locally and reduce recurring cloud API costs. However, their starting price of $4,499 must be weighed against the savings for each workload.

item.title: Google’s AI Mode Adds Temporary Threads
item.description: Google’s AI Mode temporary threads hide conversations from visible search history and disable personalization. However, discussions may still be retained for about two months.

item.title: Security Tests Show AI Models Classifying Civilians as Military Targets
item.description: Commercial AI models classified a real elementary school and civilians as military targets. Vals’ tests show that game framing and weak technical safeguards can bypass providers’ policies.

item.title: The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
item.description: Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.

item.title: Differentiation Isn’t Enough: You Need to Create Value for Customers
item.description: Being different from competitors does not mean being more useful to customers. Companies must differentiate themselves on the criteria their customers actually value, using tools such as the Strategy Canvas and the Value Proposition Canvas.

item.title: Automate sales prospecting
item.description: The article presents methods for automating sales prospecting.

item.title: Jensen Huang is worth $1 trillion to Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang’s value to Nvidia amounts to $1 trillion, something the board could not ignore.
